primary_question: Does adding nominal memory operand bytes to the v11 static latency estimate improve held-out CPP20 native CPU prediction on one pinned AMD Milan CPU?
fit: Fit each model to CPP20 training cases only, with no intercept. One row per program/input, componentwise median counter values and median of seven native CPU times in ns. Minimize the unweighted sum across training cases of squared (prediction/target - 1), coefficients nonnegative. Enumerate independent active-column subsets and solve their normal equations exactly, prefer fewer nonzero coefficients on ties, then earlier feature order. Report training matrix rank and all-zero/collinear columns. A boundary coefficient fixed to zero in an underdetermined model does not identify its true cost.

secondary_source.training: Previously fitted on three scales each of Rust integer and copy. Apply frozen rational ns coefficients to CPP20 without refitting; this tests transfer across binaries, languages and sessions.

native.target: median of seven retained native controls
native.sensitivity: minimum native time using the same median-target-fitted coefficients (no refit)
native.spread: (max - min)/median; retain and flag every failed floor or spread gate

accuracy.case_pass: Both metered predictions must fall within the inclusive tolerance. Use the exact rational prediction and target for classification. Report signed relative errors per repetition, median/min/max native controls, counter ranges, worst absolute error and counts by split. All non-training cases are held out. Report the original and additional subsets separately.
accuracy.training_support: For all counter columns report min/max case medians across training; flag each held-out feature outside its training range. The MOVS/STOS model uses the live-compatible formula but locally fitted diagnostic coefficients, never a deployed policy.

implied_boundaries.strictness: TLE iff time_ns > limit_ms * 1000000; equality passes. Do not simulate a limit unless the median lies strictly between the two integer-ms limits.
implied_boundaries.aggregation: For each boundary compare the two predictions and seven observed native CPU durations. A mixture of native outcomes is ambiguous. Any disagreement with unanimous native controls marks that case-limit as incorrect. Split into false TLE and false pass, record repetition counts and mixed predicted results. Time budgets are calculated offline from uncapped runs; no live stopped verdicts are measured.

qualification: Not a production verdict qualification. One host, eight programs, repeated sizes within each algorithm; present absolute counts, native variability and observed extrema; do not pool repetitions as independent cases or select a model on the held-out cases.
